newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria central bank says will contain inflation.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria central bank says will contain inflation.

text.p: Nigeria's central bank on Wednesday said that while the release of long-awaited government budget funds would cause a sharp rise in liquidity, measures were in place to ensure inflation would not rise.

"When funds are released in one block instead of gradually it is to be expected that there will be a sharp rise in liquidity," the central bank's director of foreign operations Mahe Rasheed told Reuters in Lagos.
"These funds were forseen in the budget and our policy of maintaining low inflation should not be affected."

The News Agency of Nigeria on Monday reported that the finance ministry had released 32.8 billion naira ($397.6 million), from the 89 billion naira ($1,072 million) budgeted for capital projects in 1997.
Rasheed would not say exactly what measures would be used to keep inflation at bay. The bank's usual means of influencing liquidity is through its weekly sales of treasury bills.

It also intervenes on the foreign exchange market at weekly auctions, which effectively determine the value of the naira currency, although the bank insists that its policy is to follow market trends.
In just over a month the naira has appreciated to 83 naira to the dollar from 85 naira to the dollar at auction.
"I do not expect any influence on the strength of the naira from the increase in liquidity," Rasheed said.
